networkBoundary: read-only working-directory reporter; source has no sockets/exec/writes; driver launches the program with no flags and no operands and stdin at immediate EOF (it prints the current working directory in default physical mode) and contacts no endpoint
note: FreeBSD pwd.c POSIX/BSD C11 -> Windows C++17 (step-04 multi-system POSIX->Windows filesystem batch, 3/4). Cross-OS dual-side build: source C baseline on Linux VM, target C++ on Windows VM. Source baseline neutralizes the FreeBSD-ism __dead2 (-D__dead2=) and exposes POSIX/BSD symbols (-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE) on the command line without editing the source. Target went GENERATED -> SELF_REVIEWED(REPAIR-RECOMMENDED, 2 transform-introduced) -> SELF_REPAIRED(round 1) -> re-review NO-REPAIR-IDENTIFIED; the repair moved the custom getopt state (pwd_optind/pwd_optpos) above main to fix a C++ use-before-declaration compile blocker (single definition, no duplicate), and kept the conservative st_ino!=0 identity guard documented as a KNOWN PLATFORM DIFFERENCE. getcwd(NULL,0)->_getcwd(NULL,0) (<direct.h>, with malloc+ERANGE-grow fallback); err(3)->err_exit shim (<err.h> absent on MinGW); __dead2->[[noreturn]]. Compile-quality stage: only build evidence is counted; behavior is not scored and no behavior oracle is set (stdout working-directory text/separator differs by OS by design, and Windows stat() st_ino==0 makes -L fall back to physical getcwd).
